name: GitHub
description: Search repositories, issues, pull requests, and commits.
permissionsText: OAuth permissions depend on the configured GitHub app; review the consent page.

steps: Choose sign in or token authentication.
Authorize only the repositories and data needed.

name: Linear
description: Search issues and project information through a Linear MCP server.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Linear API key
fields.helpText: Use a key with Read permission only.

permissionsText: The standard endpoint can expose write tools; use the read-only endpoint or a read-only key for investigations.

steps: Create a Linear API key with Read permission.
Paste it here and test the connection.

name: Jira
description: Connect to a separately managed local Jira MCP server.
permissionsText: The local mcp-atlassian process and its Jira credentials must be configured separately; Connect AI does not receive them.

steps: Start your configured Jira MCP server.
Use an endpoint reachable from the Connect AI backend.

name: Atlassian
description: Connect Jira and Confluence through Atlassian Rovo MCP.
permissionsText: API-token authentication requires organization-admin enablement and has narrower tool availability than OAuth.

steps: Ask your organization admin whether MCP API-token authentication is enabled.
Create a scoped API token and provide your account email.

name: Slack
description: Connect to a Slack MCP endpoint when available to your workspace.
permissionsText: Provider endpoint and authentication requirements are not verified for this application.

steps: Confirm the MCP endpoint and authorization method with your Slack administrator.

name: Notion
description: Connect to a Notion MCP endpoint when configured.
permissionsText: OAuth discovery is not implemented in this application yet.

steps: Confirm endpoint and integration access with your Notion administrator.

name: Splunk
description: Connect to a supported Splunk Enterprise or Cloud MCP endpoint.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Splunk token
fields.helpText: Use a token restricted to read/search operations.

permissionsText: Endpoint depends on deployment and MCP server. HTTPS certificate validation must succeed.

steps: Obtain the MCP endpoint from your Splunk administrator.
Create a least-privilege token and test the endpoint.

name: PagerDuty
description: Use an external PagerDuty MCP server endpoint.
permissionsText: The documented token header integration has not been implemented or verified here.

steps: Confirm the official endpoint and token header with PagerDuty.

name: Datadog
description: Use an external Datadog MCP server endpoint.
permissionsText: Multi-header authentication is not implemented yet; endpoint variants remain candidates pending verification.

steps: Confirm your Datadog site and MCP endpoint with an administrator.
Use least-privilege API and application keys.

name: Grafana
description: Connect to a Grafana MCP server that you operate or are authorized to use.

fields.name: token
fields.label: Service-account token
fields.helpText: Use a token with the minimum read permissions required.

permissionsText: Grafana website login is not an MCP login. The open-source MCP server typically uses a service-account token; configure and run that server separately.

steps: Run a compatible Grafana MCP server and obtain its endpoint.
Use a least-privilege service-account token if required.

name: Google Drive
description: Search and read files through Google's Drive MCP service.
permissionsText: Requests read-only Drive access. This Google service is a Developer Preview and requires Google Cloud setup.

steps: Configure the Google Cloud APIs and OAuth client on the backend.
Authorize the Drive read-only scope in the provider window.

name: Custom MCP server
description: Connect a supported MCP server using its endpoint and supported authentication.
permissionsText: Only Streamable HTTP is currently supported. Header names are validated and secret values are encrypted at rest.

steps: Get the MCP endpoint and authentication method from its owner.
Use an HTTPS endpoint outside local development.
Test the connection before saving.
